Nxeon hosting platform admin portal. Next.js/TypeScript, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`). ## The ask (from the owner, given earlier and not yet built) The admin portal's left sidebar needs: 1. Collapsible/expandable nav GROUPS (click a group header like "Marketing" or "Revenue" to collapse/expand its entries) — this doesn't exist today, only a whole-sidebar collapse toggle exists. 2. Reorganize: give "Cold Email" its own clearly-separated section, give "Mail" (the transactional-mail admin tool, distinct from Cold Email) its own top-level submenu, move "Content" into the "Marketing" group, rename the "System" label to "Settings". 3. Persist each group's collapsed/expanded state across sessions (localStorage, matching the existing pattern already used for the whole-sidebar collapse). ## Exact files and current structure (from prior research this session — verified, use directly) - **`lib/admin-groups.ts`** — the admin nav data/IA config, exports `ADMIN_NAV: AdminGroup[]`. Each `AdminGroup` is `{ key, label?, entries: AdminEntry[] }`; each `AdminEntry` is `{ key, label, icon, tabs: SubTabItem[] }` (the sidebar shows one row per entry; `tabs[0]` is the row's link, `tabs[1..]` become a horizontal sub-tab bar on the page — there is NO nested/expandable sidebar tree today, collapse only makes sense at the GROUP level). - **`components/portal/Shell.tsx`** — renders the actual sidebar. Section headers are currently a plain `

` with no click handler (around the `{section.label}` render) — no chevron, no expand/collapse affordance, you're adding this from scratch. The existing whole-rail collapse lives here too: a `useState` hydrated from `localStorage` on mount, written back on toggle, key `"nxeon.portal.railCollapsed"`, values `"1"`/`"0"`, wrapped in try/catch — mirror this exact pattern but generalize to a per-group map, e.g. `localStorage["nxeon.admin.navCollapsed"] = JSON.stringify({ marketing: true, fleet: false, ... })` keyed by each group's `key` from `admin-groups.ts`, read once on mount, updated per-header click. - **`app/admin/layout.tsx`** — server component that reads `ADMIN_NAV`, filters by feature flags/RBAC, computes badge roll-ups, maps into the generic `NavSection[]` shape `Shell` expects. You may need to thread the group `key` through this mapping if it isn't already present on the shape `Shell` consumes. - **`components/admin/SubTabs.tsx`** — the horizontal sub-tab pill bar for a multi-tab entry, unrelated to this change, don't touch. **Current `marketing` group contents** (lines ~175-263 of `lib/admin-groups.ts` as of this research) — Cold Email is ALREADY split into 6 focused entries here (`coldemail`, `coldemail-leads`, `coldemail-campaigns`, `coldemail-identity`, `coldemail-deliverability`, `coldemail-suppression`) alongside `marketing` and `studio` entries. This satisfies "Cold Email its own section" reasonably well already — read the current file to confirm this is still the state, and leave this part alone unless you find it's regressed. **Current `platform` group** (lines ~299-353) contains, among its entries: `content` (Blog/Testimonials/Newsletter/Broadcast tabs), `mail` (Inbox/Deliverability/Mailboxes/Email templates tabs — this is the transactional-mail admin tool, distinct from cold email), `system` (Settings/Automation/Staff/Logs/Audit tabs), `improvements`, `board`. **What to actually change**: - Move the `content` entry object out of `platform`'s `entries` array into `marketing`'s `entries` array (e.g. after `studio`). - Pull the `mail` entry out of `platform` into its own new top-level `AdminGroup` (e.g. `{ key: "mail", label: "Mail", entries: [ {...the existing mail entry...} ] }`) — mirror how `agency`/`ads` are already single-entry top-level groups in this file. - After removing `content` and `mail` from `platform`, that group is left with `system`/`improvements`/`board`. Rename it to read "Settings": either relabel the `platform` group's `label` from "Platform" to "Settings", or rename just the `system` entry's label from "System" to "Settings" — read the current file structure once `content`/`mail` are removed and use your judgment for whichever produces the cleaner-looking result (the owner said "rename System to Settings," and given Content/Mail are leaving, renaming the group label is likely the closer match to intent, but check first). ## Build the collapsible UI In `Shell.tsx`: add a click handler + chevron icon to each group's section-label header, toggling that group's entries visibility, sourced from and persisted to the localStorage map described above (default: all expanded, so existing behavior is unchanged for anyone with no saved state). Respect existing styling conventions in the file (don't introduce a new design language — match the site's existing sidebar look). ## Verification `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean. If Playwright or similar is available, click through: expand/collapse a couple of groups, reload the page, confirm state persisted; confirm Cold Email/Mail/Content/Settings all show correctly. If no browser automation is available, at least visually sanity-check via a screenshot of the admin sidebar if you can get an authenticated admin session (check how other agents this session logged into `/admin` for screenshots, if any precedent exists) — otherwise a clean build + careful code review is the fallback. ## Build safety `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-adminnav -b feature/admin-sidebar-reorg`, symlink `node_modules`/`.env`, work only there, never build in the live `/opt/nxeon` tree. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging/production — this changes navigation for every admin page, so it should be reviewed before going live. Commit on the branch and stop. Report back: the final `ADMIN_NAV` structure (a quick summary of which group has which entries now), commit hash, and confirmation that build/typecheck are clean.

363	 * (`/admin/users/123`). The bare "/admin" only ever matches exactly so it can
364	 * never swallow every deeper route.
365	 */
366	export function hrefMatches(href: string, pathname: string): boolean {
367	  if (pathname === href) return true;
368	  if (href === "/admin") return false;
369	  return pathname.startsWith(href + "/");
370	}
371	
372	/**
373	 * Resolve which top-level entry owns a given admin pathname, by longest
374	 * matching member href. Returns null for admin paths outside the IA.
375	 */
376	export function entryForPath(pathname: string): AdminEntry | null {
377	  let best: { entry: AdminEntry; len: number } | null = null;
378	  for (const entry of adminEntries()) {
379	    for (const tab of entry.tabs) {
380	      if (hrefMatches(tab.href, pathname) && (!best || tab.href.length > best.len)) {
381	        best = { entry, len: tab.href.length };
382	      }
383	    }
384	  }
385	  return best?.entry ?? null;

## Report **Worktree:** `/opt/nxeon-wt-adminnav`, branch `feature/admin-sidebar-reorg`, commit `1adc5df` (`node_modules` symlinked, `.env` copied, no build/merge/deploy done in the live tree or main). ### `lib/admin-groups.ts` — final `ADMIN_NAV` structure (9 sections, 25 entries, no hrefs changed) 1. **(unlabeled lead-in)** — Overview 2. **Customers** — Clients, Support 3. **Fleet** — Servers, Infrastructure, Operations, Domains 4. **Revenue** — Billing, Catalog, Promotions 5. **Marketing** — Marketing, Studio, **Content** (moved in from Platform), then the existing 6-way Cold Email split: Cold Email, Leads, Campaigns, Sending identity, Deliverability, Suppression 6. **Agency** — Sitewave 7. **Ads** — Adloop 8. **Mail** *(new top-level group)* — Mail (Inbox/Deliverability/Mailboxes/Email templates — the transactional-mail tool, unchanged hrefs, just promoted out of Platform into its own section, mirroring how Agency/Ads are single-entry groups) 9. **Platform** — **Settings** (was "System", label renamed; same tabs: Settings/Automation/Staff/Logs/Audit), Improvements, Boards Judgment call on the "rename System to Settings" ask: renamed the *entry* label (`system` → "Settings") rather than the group label, since that's the literal element the owner referred to; left the `platform` group label as-is since it still sensibly covers Settings/Improvements/Boards after Content and Mail left. ### `components/portal/Shell.tsx` - Added `key?: string` to `NavSection`. - Added per-group collapse state (`collapsedGroups`), hydrated once from `localStorage["nxeon.admin.navCollapsed"]` (JSON map of group key → collapsed bool) and written back on every toggle, wrapped in try/catch — same pattern as the existing `nxeon.portal.railCollapsed` whole-rail toggle. - Section headers are now a clickable button with a chevron (rotates on collapse) **only in the admin portal** (`isAdminPortal`); the customer dashboard's headers are untouched (still plain `

`, no behavior change there). - When the whole rail is icon-collapsed, per-group collapse is ignored so every icon row stays reachable (no dead-end state). - Default state is all-expanded, so existing sessions see no visual change until they use the new toggle. ### `app/admin/layout.tsx` - Threaded `key: section.key` into the `NavSection[]` mapping so `Shell` can key its collapse-state map to the same stable keys used in `admin-groups.ts`. ### Verification - `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, no errors. - `npm run build` — completed with exit code 0, no compile errors (checked full output for `Failed`/`Error`). - No authenticated browser session was available in this run (no Playwright/precedent found), so visual confirmation of the sidebar was not done — clean build + typecheck + code review is the fallback, as the task allowed. Branch is committed and left as-is; nothing was merged or pushed.
